title: Bankruptcy discharge - basics
facts: A bankruptcy discharge releases the debtor from personal liability for debts covered by the discharge and generally prohibits creditors from taking collection action on those discharged debts.
Not all debts are dischargeable, and discharge rules differ among bankruptcy chapters.

A discharge generally does not automatically remove a valid lien from collateral; a secured creditor may retain rights against the property unless the lien is avoided or otherwise addressed under bankruptcy law.
A discharge can be denied or revoked in specified circumstances involving failure to comply with bankruptcy requirements or misconduct.
